entities.summary: Walter of Mortagne was a Scholastic philosopher and Catholic theologian of the High Middle Ages. Born in the 12th century, Mortagne studied at the University of Paris, where he developed a distinctive intellectual approach. He was particularly interested in the relationship between faith and reason, and his writings had a significant impact on the development of Scholasticism. Mortagne's work was widely admired by his contemporaries, including Thomas Becket, who later became Archbishop of Canterbury. The theologian's influence can be seen in the writings of later medieval thinkers, such as Duns Scotus. Despite the passage of centuries, Walter of Mortagne's ideas continue to be studied by scholars today. His legacy is a testament to the enduring power of intellectual curiosity and the pursuit of knowledge. As the 12th-century historian, William of Newburgh, noted, Mortagne's 'excellent memory' and 'prodigious' learning made him 'one of the most learned men of his time'.
